title: Guy Kelly, drinking and Louis Armstrong's regard for him
summary: Vincent says Guy Kelly was not much recognized by Louis, recalls his death, and talks about liquor and rehearsals.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Louis couldn't believe it. Louis used to recognize Guy Kelly, didn't it? Louis, didn't he recognize Guy Kelly? Uh, not much. No. Everybody say Guy Kelly was next to him. No. I was with Guy when he died. When he left here, he was good. But when he got up there, he got so he couldn't play nothing much. Uh, you know what I meant to lick it? I know. I want to see what I'm talking about. You used to sit like that? I played caps at his funeral. He did die just that time about four times, not behind one another. And then Paul used to bring in a little license, buy the jar and then give it to Guy. And when me and Guy, precious of here, he got his precious of here, down there and get that pair of some nachos and stuff. But he's another liquor here. And Joe Roe was here. Joe Roe, he wasn't so much on liquor, you know. And I could drink some of that stuff, he could make me sick. And I had to lay off it, you know. Then when I'd get around there, I'd have to try to drink to be sociable, you know. I couldn't make it all the time, you know. But Guy, well, we used to go to rehearsals, and put my head on a garage that big, and just put it over that light and he got it. Got it on. I'd be like, step into all these inside of them.
